text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper may move to test resistance at $2,300 a tonne following late gains on Thursday, traders and analysts said.
A break above $2,300 could spark a move towards $2,330.
Aluminium needs to breach resistance above $1,580 to spark a move to $1,600, they added.
COPPER - Thursday's late rally has helped to bolster upside chart sentiment but prices need to overcome $2,300 resistance to spark further confidence and gains, traders and chartists said on Friday.

London Metal Exchange (LME) brokers Brandeis said Thursday's chart close was fairly positive which helped to offset some of this week's losses. "The market needs to breach $2,300, however, to move higher and will then look to fill the gap between $2,365 and $2,308," Brandeis said.
Harry Creates of Amalgamated Trading said copper could test resistance at $2,302, with a close above this level targeting $2,330 and $2,360.
On the downside Creates pegged support at $2,250, $2,230 and $2,210.
At 0753 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,266/70, against Thursday's late London close of $2,285/87.

ALUMINIUM - Initial resistance seen at levels around $1,580. "Thursday's chart picture suggests indecision about moving higher," Brandeis said. "Good resistance is seen around the $1,583/85 area where there is a small gap on the chart," they added.
On the downside Creates of AMT pegged support at $1,555 and $1,542.
At 0753 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,561/63, versus $1,569/70. --London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
